newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-FAIRYTALE CONTINUES AS CHESTERFIELD REACH CUP SEMIFINAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FAIRYTALE CONTINUES AS CHESTERFIELD REACH CUP SEMIFINAL.

text.p: Second division Chesterfield enjoyed the greatest day in their largely uneventful 131-year history when they beat Wrexham 1-0 to reach the semifinals of the English F.A. Cup for the first time on Sunday.

The only goal of a tense, exciting quarter-final against their fellow second division rivals came after 58 minutes and was scored by 31-year-old journeyman striker Chris Beaumont who signed for Chesterfied for a bargain price of 22,500 pounds ($36,000) from Stockport County last summer.
He chased down a long ball from Andy Morris and as Wrexham goalkeeper Andrew Marriott and defender Deryn Brace each left the ball for the other to clear, Beaumont nipped in between them to score.
Chesterfield had two more chances with Beaumont hitting the post four minutes later and Marriott denying Jonathon Howard's close-range shot a minute later.

But although they could not find the net again, Chesterfield had done enough to become the first side from the third tier of English football to reach the semifinals in 13 years and only the seventh in the cup's 125-year history.
No club from that level has ever reached the final.

Chesterfield manager John Duncan said: "That was the longest half-hour of my life after the goal was scored. But I think we deserved it, we kept our cool in the first half and took the chance when it came in the second. I am exhausted, and utterly, utterly delighted."

At the end of the game the home supporters swarmed on to the pitch and lifted the players shoulder-high. Older fans were crying tears of joy and the local radio switchboard was jammed as thousands of supporters tried to express their delight on air.
"The whole town's alight, I've waited 40 years for this, everyone knows about Chesterfield now," said one ecstatic caller.

Chesterfield's unlikely cup journey began with a first round 1-0 victory over Bury on November 16. Since then they have beaten Scarborough (2-0), Bristol City (2-0), Bolton Wanderers (3-2), and premier league Nottingham Forest (1-0).
Wrexham, who came into the match after impressive wins over Birmingham City and West Ham, dominated the opening half-hour but failed to turn their midfield superiority into goal advantage.

Whenever they did get forward Chesterfield goalkeeper Billy Mercer was outstanding, except for one near-calamatious mistake late in the match when he lost control of the ball and almost presented a Wrexham striker with an open goal.
Wrexham, bidding to reach the semifinals for the first time themselves, could have no complaints about losing.
Wrexham manager Brian Flynn said: "It wasn't to be, was it? I can't complain about our effort but we just did not make enough chances and in the end that cost us."
Chesterfield join Middlesbrough, 2-0 winners over Derby on Saturday, in the cup semifinals.
In the other quarter-finals, Chelsea were leading Portsmouth 2-0 at halftime and Sheffield Wednesday were playing Wimbledon later on Sunday.
